title: Resolution and geometric coherence of closed-test section models
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and on every small pro-etale site put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal $\Lambda_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their exact inverse images and ordinary unbounded derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. All sites and section values are taken in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$ an ideal, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak a)\hookrightarrow U$. Let $v$ be the affine ind-etale closed-site lift [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Let $V\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object such that $V$ and $B=v(V)$ are w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Let $f:X\to U$ be a morphism of affine schemes and put $X_Z=X\times_UZ$, with projections $h:X_Z\to X$, $f_Z:X_Z\to Z$. Put $T=X\times_UB$, $T_0=X\times_UV$ and $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$; products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a K-injective representative $\mathcal I$ of $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ and a K-injective resolution $j:h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$, use the normalized source model $C=Q(\mathcal I(T))$ and target model $D=Q(\mathcal J(T_0))$. Normalize the source comparison by the inverse of the actual unit-section map $(f_*\mathcal I)(B)\to(s^*f_*\mathcal I)(V)$, the target comparison by the direct-image section identity, and both localized-section comparisons by the degreewise identity. Put $r=Q(j(T_0)\circ\eta_a):C\to D$, where $\eta_a$ is the actual inverse-image unit section [def-sfb-proetale-inverse-image-unit-section].
These comparisons and $r$ are independent of both resolutions, with transition maps induced by the unique homotopy classes of comparisons into K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. They are natural for every morphism $K\to K'$: if $c,d$ are the induced source and target maps, then $d\circ r=r'\circ c$, and the same transition maps commute with the derived section comparisons. Homotopic comparison maps give identical arrows in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$.
For any map $V'\to V$ with both tests and their lifts w-contractible, the analogous square for $r$ and the section-model comparisons commutes, with $c,d$ the presheaf restriction maps on the fibre products. The same equations hold for an isomorphism of the original cartesian square. They also hold after any pro-etale base change $U'\to U$, on affine localizations and every admissible test there, using the induced site localizations, pullback composition and the canonical derived direct-image composition comparisons. In this last assertion the localized direct-image comparison is normalized by $(f_*F)(W)=F(X\times_UW)$ and commutes with the localized adjunction units and counits. Compatibility is asserted with these specified comparison maps; it imposes no invertibility on the closed restriction.

proof.text: Use the concrete maps of [def-sfb-closed-test-localized-model-data]. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-comparison-normalization] for the pinned source and target isomorphisms and for invertibility of the two localization units. The inverse equations show sourceUnit and targetUnit invertible as inverses of the supplied isomorphisms.

Use [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison] to represent α into I′ and Qj inverse followed by h*α and Qj′ into J′. Injectivity gives the comparison homotopy. Additive evaluation carries it to a homotopy; naturality of unitAt proves the model-arrow square. Naturality of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and exact-pullback factors gives all comparison squares. Homotopic maps have equal Q-images and isomorphic α gives invertible evaluated transitions by conjugating with the derived units.

Apply [lem-sfb-closed-test-comparison-test-naturality] for the five test-map squares, using the same global I, J and j on both tests. This proves TestCoherence independently of the already established resolution changes.

Use [lem-sfb-closed-test-localized-restriction-normalization], [lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-comparison-normalization] and [lem-sfb-closed-test-geometric-section-coherence] for the normalized localized model equation, specified comparison isomorphisms, and the full geometric localization statement including its mate unit/counit equations. Assemble these with the proved resolution-independence conjunction and the five test squares.
